definition: An AVL tree is a binary search tree that rebalances after every insert and delete so the heights of a node's two subtrees differ by at most one. Rotations restore that balance. Search, insert, and delete are logarithmic in the worst case, at the cost of more rotations than a red-black tree.

complexity.time: Search, insert, and delete are O(log n) in the worst case.
complexity.space: O(n) space for the elements themselves.

examples: An ordered index that must not degrade after sorted inserts
